top_choice_rationale: P001 recognises the optical lattice clock, a distinct invention (magic-wavelength trapping of many neutral atoms, trap light shift cancelled) that is separate from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion prizes. Its 1e-18 performance is reproduced by independent laboratories and clock-to-clock links, which is the evidence I weight most, and the Katori and Ye allocation is clean, with the citation scoped to the magic-wavelength lattice rather than to accuracy in general. P002 comes next because it still awards the clock but adds a one-name IceCube credit for a very large collaboration that I cannot defend. P003 is a mature, well-reproduced experimental achievement, but the three-of-five credit choice is contested. No award ranks last because the clock is ready.
recusal_note: Distant mentor link only: my PhD included a stay in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder, and JILA is Ye's institution. No collaboration with Katori or Ye, so no recusal apparent, but disclosed. Also an institutional WACQT link to Chalmers.
